text:
Incident Bot: [P1] High GPU queue growth in us-west1-prod. Autoscale attempts failing, throttling observed. Pager: oncall-eng. thread_ts=2037004321
Maya Patel: I'm on call — looking. Thanks for the ping. What services are impacted?
Samir K: batch-infer and realtime-gen queues both spiking. queue_length=6200 avg_wait_ms=1200 token_throttle=1.2% errors=504
Lee Wong: seeing similar on metrics dashboard — 95th latency up from 120ms -> 2.3s. Autoscaler events show repeated ScaleUpFailed errors.
Samir K: paste: 
```
Autoscaler: failed to increase GPU nodes: quotaExceeded or placementError
Event: NotTriggerScaling - insufficient resources for pod(s): could not find available GPU due to fragmentation
```
Maya Patel: hmm fragmentation + MIG sizing mismatch? Any nodes with leftover MIG slices?
Jon R.: I'm joining — grabbing logs. We have mixed MIG profiles: some nodes have 1xA100-40GB, others have 4xA100-10GB slices. Scheduler can't pack large 40GB pods onto nodes with only 10GB slices, leaving small unusable capacity. That leaves whole GPUs stranded.
Samir K: confirmed: 37 GPUs reported as "available" by node-level inventory but scheduler rejects because pod requests 16GB contiguous and only 12GB contiguous free in many nodes. Binpacking failing.
Maya Patel: immediate mitigation options?
Lee Wong: quick wins: 1) pause low-priority batch queues 2) temporarily route heavy realtime to Dedicated pool (if available) 3) manual node reclamation: cordon + drain mismatched nodes and rebuild them with a consistent MIG profile.
Maya Patel: executing step 1 now — placing batch-infer queue on hold via rate limiter. @Jose (CS) please communicate to affected customers ASAP.
Jose (CS): notifying top 10 customers, message drafted: "We're seeing inference latency increases due to GPU placement issues; mitigation in progress. We will follow up with ETA."
Autoscaler Bot: attempted scale up to +12 GPU nodes at 2037004410 — failed due to project GPU quota limit in us-west1 (current=128, requested=140).
Jon R.: quota is part of it. Also autoscaler appears to retry but misclassifies placement errors as capacity shortage leading to throttle loops. We need infra to raise quota or temporarily shift traffic region.
oncall-infra: acknowledged. Increasing quota request submitted to cloud ops; ETA ~35 minutes. Can also spin a small pool in us-central as fallback.
Maya Patel: while quota increases, I'll attempt manual rebalance to free contiguous slices: plan — identify nodes with mixed MIGs, cordon & drain non-critical pods, recreate nodes with uniform MIG profile (16GB or 32GB) so scheduler can place.
Samir K: command snippets I've run: 
```
kubectl get nodes -l gpu=true -o json | jq '.items[] | {name:.metadata.name, mig_profiles:.status.allocatable}'
kubectl cordon gpu-node-17 && kubectl drain gpu-node-17 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
gcloud compute instances reset gpu-node-17 --metadata mig-profile=1g.16gb
```
Maya Patel: doing staged drains now. Draining node gpu-node-17 (low-prio pods only). If drain takes >2m we'll abort and rollback.
Lee Wong: note: draining causes short-lived evictions and may increase queue backlog briefly. Keep rate limiter on.
Jon R.: I see new placements succeeding on nodes recreated with 32GB profile. Realtime error rate dropping from 12% -> 4% in first 6 mins.
Maya Patel: handoff to Jon in 10m for remediation & post-incident. @Jon R. take over?
Jon R.: taking. I'll keep the runbook open: "gpu-placement-rebalance". Next steps: finish rebuilding 6 nodes, coordinate quota bump, change autoscaler policy to prefer creation of uniform-profile instances, add circuit-breaker to avoid retry storms on placement errors.
Maya Patel: Customer impact summary for incident timeline: 2037004321 - 2037004600: 12% of realtime token requests saw 5xx; ~8 customer accounts reported degraded performance; batch jobs delayed by ~45-120m.
Jose (CS): customers updated at 2037004450; will post follow-up when stabilized.
Jon R.: leaving follow-ups: create an alert for "scheduler placement failures" separate from generic node insufficiency, add a reclamation job to periodically detect and consolidate MIG slices, and update capacity planning docs to avoid mixed MIG fleets in prod.
Maya Patel: adding retrospective owners: infra for quota & autoscaler fixes, eng-runtime for scheduler heuristics, devex for runbook updates, cs for customer comms.
Incident Bot: incident state: mitigated -> reduced impact; monitoring for 2 hours. Incident severity will be reviewed by SRE.
Jon R.: closing handoff note: I have control of scaling actions and will not remove any more nodes without cross-checking with CS. If anything else triggers, page me directly.
Lee Wong: metrics stabilizing. 95th latency back to ~180ms, token failure rate <1.5%.
Jose (CS): customers acknowledging updates and grateful for quick mitigation.
Maya Patel: thanks everyone. Postmortem owners: Jon R. (lead), Samir K (data), Lee Wong (metrics), Infra (quota). We'll open a postmortem ticket and schedule blameless review.
